subject: On-prem vs Dedicated: solutioning notes + acceptance criteria request
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Lina Ortiz <lina.ortiz@genexmed.com>
Cc: Procurement <procure@genexmed.com>
Date: 2027-04-18T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Follow-up: private deployment options and immediate asks

Hi Lina — thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our discovery call and a few asks so we can size and scope properly: 

Summary of alternatives we discussed:
- Hosted API: fastest to production, no hardware footprint at GenexMed, but not acceptable if you require air-gapped operations.
- Dedicated capacity (Redwood Dedicated): reserved GPU pools in our cloud region with network isolation and SLA; good middle-ground if outbound is allowed for control-plane / telemetry.
- Private (VPC / on-prem appliance): fully isolated deployment we manage with optional on-site appliance or VM bundle; supports air-gapped operations but requires HW & ops planning.

Key items we need to proceed with a Private/air-gapped quote:
1) Confirmation that the environment must be fully air-gapped (no outbound egress) — you mentioned this is likely but wanted to confirm.
2) Expected concurrency / QPS for model inferencing (tokens/sec, typical prompt sizes).
3) Hardware constraints: rack space, power per rack (kW), available PDU type, and preferred GPU family (if you have procurement constraints).
4) Upgrade / maintenance policy: planned quarterly maintenance windows acceptable? Do you require field upgrades to be performed only during scheduled blackouts?
5) SOC2 / audit evidence points we should prepare (we can pre-send an evidence pack).

Attached a short qualification form (fill the hardware fields) and our on-prem checklist so your infra team can annotate.

Next steps / ask: could you share the filled form and a preferred time for a short 30-min follow-up with your infra and procurement (we propose Wed or Thu next week)? Once we get the form, we’ll prepare a preliminary BOM and a draft mutual action plan with acceptance criteria (SLA, throughput test, upgrade MOP).

Thanks — happy to jump on a call to walk through the checklist.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
(415) 555-0148

Attachments: genexmed-qualification-form.pdf (PDF - 2 pages); redwood-onprem-checklist-v1.xlsx (Excel - 1 sheet)

From: Lina Ortiz <lina.ortiz@genexmed.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-19T09:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: private deployment options and immediate asks

Hi Marissa — thanks for the clear recap and the checklist. Confirming the following from our side: 

- Air-gap requirement: yes, GenexMed requires a fully air-gapped solution for any PHI-adjacent workloads. No outbound connections allowed from inference hosts. Control-plane interaction must go over an approved, one-way removable media process or a tightly controlled NAT device inside our DMZ (we will provide details).
- Maintenance windows: quarterly maintenance windows are acceptable. For security patches that are critical we will allow emergency patching but require documented MOP and signed approval from our Security Ops lead.
- Hardware: our baseline preference is a dense A100-ish rack (we currently have vendors quoting 8xA100 80GB per rack), but procurement is evaluating cost/availability. Please propose both an A100-caliber and an A10/A30-caliber configuration for comparison.
- Throughput: initial pilot target is ~60 concurrent users, average prompt 1–2k tokens, expected steady-state ~30 requests/minute per rack for the pilot. We'll share more accurate telemetry after procurement provides environment specs.

I’ve attached the partially filled qualification PDF (see notes on power and rack units). Procurement (procure@genexmed.com) is looped for budget/schedule coordination.

Preferred follow-up times: Thu 2027-04-22 10:00–12:00 PT. Please send an invite if that works.

Regards,
Lina Ortiz
Head, ML Infrastructure | GenexMed
lina.ortiz@genexmed.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-19T10:08:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Follow-up: private deployment options and immediate asks

Team — forwarding GenexMed’s confirmation and partial form. Key callouts: full air-gap, preference for A100-class but procurement wants cost options, pilot throughput ~30 rps/min overall (see Lina’s numbers).

Action items I’m assigning: 
- Ben: can you run a quick BOM for both an A100 and an A10 configuration (include rack U, estimated power, and a standby redundancy plan)? Also flag any components that require cloud access for sanity checks (we need true offline upgrade paths).
- Tessa: prepare an ops MOP for offline upgrades (step-by-step, including how to safely inject new model binaries via removable media) and a maintenance SLAs doc we can present to security.
- Karthik: review model size/weights assumptions for memory/KV cache; identify whether we need NVMe-backed KV and approximate storage sizing for 512-token context windows at scale.

Schedule: Lina proposed Thu 2027-04-22 10–12 PT for a follow-up. Can we get a 30-min internal sync tomorrow to align on the draft BOM and MOP before I join the customer call?

I’ve attached the customer-completed qualification form and our onprem checklist with Lina’s notes. Please reply-all with ETA so I can confirm internal sync and then lock the customer invite.

Thanks — Marissa

Attachments (forwarded): genexmed-qualification-form.pdf; redwood-onprem-checklist-v1.xlsx

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-20T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Follow-up: private deployment options and immediate asks

Marissa / team — quick notes after a 25-min pass on Lina’s inputs: 

1) BOM roughs (ETA EOD today for a cleaned doc):
  - A100-class: 1 rack = 8xA100-80GB; estimated power 12.5kW; require 42U rack. Rack-level NVMe: 8x4TB recommended for KV & swap; redundant PDU recommended.
  - A10 alternative: 8xA10G or 10xA30 works at ~60% of A100 perf for inference cost; power ~10kW; smaller chassis possible.

2) Offline upgrades: agree we must design a signed-MOP process. Tessa — please use our offline upgrade template and add: checksum validation, signed manifest, air-gapped transfer steps, and rollback MOP. We should also include a staged verification (unit test model on a mirrored offline test node before push).

3) SLA / maintenance language: propose quarterly maintenance with a 7-day notice window for non-critical patches; critical security patches can be applied with Security Ops approval within 48 hours. We should add an option for an extended maintenance blackout if GenexMed requires it (chargeable).

4) Pre-flight acceptance criteria (draft):
  - Throughput validation: run a 1-hour load test that matches pilot qps with <150ms p95 on target prompts.
  - Functional validation: parity check on a 200-prompt eval set; top-line metric: <2% generation quality regression vs. hosted baseline.
  - Upgrade validation: test rollback completes within 30 minutes and preserves KV cache integrity.

I’ll produce the BOM and send a short readout by 17:00 PT. Internal sync at 11:30 PT tomorrow works for me.

—Ben
